results.title: Korea's climate ambassador to join UN climate summit in Turkey as presidential envoy
results.content: Korea's ambassador for global climate and environment will attend a U.N. climate summit set to take place in Turkey later this week as a special presidential envoy, the foreign ministry said Monday. Ambassador Kang Kum-sil will join the summit, part of the 31st Conference of the Parties to the U.N. Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), set to take place on Wednesday and Thursday in Antalya, as leaders from some 80 countries are expected to participate. Kang plans to highlight Seoul's commitment to strengthening its contribution to global efforts to combat climate change and explain its electrification and decarbonization strategies, according to the ministry. Kang, a former justice minister, was appointed to the ambassador post in January.

results.title: Lee meets Uzbek Senate speaker, hails strategic ties between 2 countries
results.content: Korean President Lee Jae Myung met with the speaker of the Uzbek Senate on Monday and hailed the special strategic relationship developing between their countries. During the meeting with Tanzila Narbaeva, chairwoman of the Senate of Uzbekistan, at Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul, Lee expressed satisfaction with the strengthening of mutually beneficial economic cooperation between the two countries, presidential spokesperson Kim Sung-wan said. The Korean president said bilateral ties are being elevated to a special strategic partnership following the state visit in September by Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Lee and Mirziyoyev held a summit in Seoul that month and agreed to strengthen cooperation in critical mineral supply chains, artificial intelligence, digital transformation and human and cultural exchanges. results.title: Deploying mine-hunting assets to anti-piracy unit meant to prepare for unseen threats: defense minister
results.content: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul said Monday that Korea's decision to expand its anti-piracy naval unit's operational scope with mine-hunting assets is aimed at preparing for potential threats near the Strait of Hormuz that "cannot be entirely ruled out." Kang made the remarks after Seoul announced plans last week to expand the operational scope of the Cheonghae Unit from the current zone in waters off the Somali coast to south of Oman in the Arabian Sea, about 650 kilometers away from the Hormuz strait. It is also seeking to deploy mine-sweeping vehicles and equipment, as well as an explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) team and the P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft. Although Seoul has stressed that the move is strictly intended to protect Korean commercial ships and citizens from piracy, critics argue it amounts to a de facto military contribution to the U.S. war with Iran. results.title: Jeon Do-yeon surprised by rave reviews for her 'Possible Love' role
results.content: Iconic actor Jeon Do-yeon, who plays the wife of a traumatized laid-off worker in the Korean film "Possible Love," said she did not expect a wave of positive reviews about her acting, saying the filming flowed very naturally. Directed by Lee Chang-dong, the film follows laid-off factory worker Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and his wife, Mi-ok (Jeon), whose lives become intertwined with documentary producer Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong) and her wealthy husband, Sang-woo (Zo In-sung). The film, which marked Lee's first feature in eight years since the critically acclaimed "Burning" (2018), won the Silver Lion Grand Jury Prize at this year's Venice International Festival Film. It marked Jeon's first collaboration with the Korean auteur in 19 years since "Secret Sunshine" (2007), which earned her the Best Actress award at the Cannes Film Festival. "I was surprised. results.title: Prison terms sought for ex-security officials for leaking THAAD-related intelligence
results.content: The prosecution on Monday sought prison terms for three officials who served under former President Moon Jae-in on charges of leaking intelligence related to the THAAD U.S. missile defense system. Prosecutors requested 10-month prison sentences for Chung Eui-yong, former national security adviser, and Jeong Kyeong-doo, former defense minister, during their trial on power abuse charges at the Seoul Central District Court. They also sought a two-year prison term for Suh Choo-suk, former first deputy national security adviser. Chung and Jeong are accused of giving orders to inform activists opposed to South Korea's hosting of the Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) system of operations to replace THAAD battery missiles and radar equipment in Seongju, 215 kilometers southeast of Seoul, in May 2020. results.title: From police intervention to celebrity fans: Seoul scarf seller becomes unlikely 'idol'
results.content: A scarf vendor at Seoul's Namdaemun Market has become an unlikely celebrity, drawing crowds so large that police have been called to the scene and private security guards hired to maintain order. His popularity has also caught the attention of Korean entertainers, some of whom have visited his stall to meet him in person. The vendor has gone viral on social media for his witty remarks, playful interactions with customers and charismatic salesmanship. His growing fan base has earned him the nickname "Namdaemun idol," turning an ordinary scarf stall at one of Seoul's oldest traditional markets into an unexpected tourist attraction. The frenzy has become so intense that the vendor temporarily closed his stall on Thursday amid safety concerns after police were called to manage the crowds. results.title: Samsung, Hyundai Motor Group join forces to lead future industries
results.content: Top executives from Samsung Electronics and Hyundai Motor Group (HMG) held a rare joint gathering, Monday, to strengthen cooperation in physical artificial intelligence (AI) and next-generation mobility technologies, signaling closer ties between two of Korea’s largest industrial groups. The meeting comes as the two conglomerates are seeking to expand cooperation beyond existing business ties in areas, such as automotive electronics, batteries and components, with a particular focus on electric vehicles (EVs), autonomous driving, software-defined vehicles (SDVs) and robotics. Samsung hosted senior Hyundai Motor Group executives at its training center in Seocheon, South Chungcheong Province, for an event dubbed HMG Appreciation Day, the first large-scale event of its kind that Samsung has held for a major Korean business group. The gathering brought together 177 executives and their spous

results.title: Defense chief signals potential shift in plans to integrate military academies
results.content: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul said Monday the government may review the location of an envisioned integrated military academy, signaling a shift in its push to establish a single institution in the central city of Daejeon amid a backlash. Kang made the remarks in a meeting with the leaders of alumni associations of the Army, Navy and Air Force, as the defense ministry's plan to integrate their academies has faced pushback from graduates and reserve forces. Under the basic plan unveiled in July, the government plans to set up a single military academy at Jaundae, a compound of military training and education facilities in Daejeon, about 140 kilometers south of Seoul. "What I can say for certain is that we are not trying to abolish each military academy," Kang said. "Education specific to each military branch surely must be in place, so long as we do not form a unified force," he added.

results.title: Korean won strengthens on dollar sales, risk-taking mood
results.content: The Korean won strengthened against the U.S. dollar Monday, helped by dollar selling by local exporters and a risk-taking mood as artificial intelligence-related jitters showed some signs of easing. The won was quoted at 1,347.1 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., up 9.5 won from the close of the previous stock trading session. At one point in the afternoon trading, the Korean currency climbed to a high of 1,346.7 won per dollar before trimming some gains. However, the won's advance was limited as foreign investors remained net sellers of local stocks for a seventh consecutive session. Foreign investors sold a net 693 billion won ($514 million) worth of local shares during the latest regular stock trading session, with the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index falling 0.81 percent to close at 5,018.85.

results.title: Korea manager hoping to see players grow at int'l baseball tournament in Tokyo
results.content: As Korea gears up for its final international baseball tournament of the year in Tokyo this week, national team manager Choi Won-ho said Monday he wanted young players to use the event as a learning experience. Choi led his team to the Japanese capital Monday afternoon for the Asia Professional Baseball Championship (APBC), which will run from Thursday to Sunday at Tokyo Dome. Japan, Australia and Taiwan are the three other participants. Korea will open the tournament against Australia at noon Thursday, and play Japan at 7 p.m. Friday. Korea will then take on Taiwan at 7 p.m. Saturday. After round-robin play, the bottom two teams will meet in the third-place match at 11 a.m. Sunday, and the final will be between the top two nations at 7 p.m. Sunday. results.title: French universities deepen ties with Korea as student interest grows
results.content: French higher education institutions are increasingly turning their attention to Korea, with participation in a major education fair in Seoul more than doubling in just two years, driven by growing interest among French students in studying in Korea. A total of 44 French institutions took part in this year's Study in France fair, organized by the French Embassy in Seoul and Campus France, up from just 20 at a similar event two years ago, according to Sébastien Codina, scientific and higher education cooperation attache at the embassy. "You cannot imagine how much young French people really love Korea," Codina told The Korea Times, pointing to the growing popularity of Korean culture in France. The expanding interest goes beyond K-pop, beauty and food, with French higher educational institutions increasingly seeking opportunities to send students to Korea and establish deeper academic par

results.title: Late Hyosung chairman honored Korea-US friendship award
results.content: Late Hyosung Group Honorary Chairman Cho Suck-rai has been posthumously awarded the Korea-America Friendship Award in recognition of his decades-long efforts to strengthen economic ties between Korea and the United States. The group said that the late chairman received the 24th annual award from the Korea-America Association (KAA) at its ceremony on Monday in Seoul, with his son, Hyosung Chairman Cho Hyun-joon, accepting the award on his behalf. The association recognized Cho Suck-rai for his efforts to strengthen bilateral economic ties, particularly his role in rallying business support for the free trade agreement between Korea and the U.S. and helping secure Korea's entry into the U.S. Visa Waiver Program. Accepting the award, Cho Hyun-joon expressed gratitude on behalf of his family, noting that his grandfather, former KAA Chairman Song In-sang, had received the same honor in 2004.

results.title: Jensen Huang affair casts shadow over Nvidia's Korea partnerships
results.content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission of a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy is raising concerns among Korean industry officials that the controversy could eventually affect the U.S. artificial intelligence (AI) giant's partnerships with Korean companies, particularly if investigations expand into potential security breaches or questions over Huang's leadership. Huang acknowledged having an extramarital affair with businesswoman Alice Huang in a message to Nvidia employees, saying he was “unfaithful” to his wife and family. New York Times first reported that U.S. intelligence officials believed that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. results.title: KOSPI barely holds 5000, fails to regain momentum
results.content: KOSPI struggled to regain its footing Monday after plunging more than 11 percent last week. The benchmark index barely held above the 5,000 mark, underscoring the volatility that has gripped the market since concerns over tighter U.S. artificial intelligence (AI) regulation rattled semiconductor stocks following the Democrats’ sweeping midterm election victory on Nov. 3. The index opened at 5,043.20, down 0.5 percent from the previous close, according to the Korea Exchange. Institutional buying, alongside a modest rebound in semiconductor heavyweights, lifted it back above 5,100 during the session. The gains proved short-lived, however, as foreign selling pushed KOSPI lower again, with the index eventually closing at 5,018.85, down 0.81 percent. results.title: Real-life Prince Heinrey? Lee Jong-suk's real estate holdings estimated at $45 mil.
results.content: A luxury home Korean actor Lee Jong-suk purchased at a steep discount more than a decade ago has reportedly surged nearly fivefold in value, contributing to a real estate portfolio now estimated at around 63 billion won. According to a video released Saturday on the YouTube channel "Wander Planet," Lee purchased a luxury residence at La Terrasse Hannam in UN Village, an exclusive residential neighborhood in Seoul's Hannam-dong, for approximately 4.3 billion won ($3 million) in March 2015. The 284-square-meter property was reportedly offered at a discount of more than 50 percent from its original sale price because of financial difficulties faced by its developer, Dongyang Group. The estimated market value of a comparable unit has since climbed to around 20 billion won, representing a gain of approximately 15.7 billion won. results.title: Abandoned schools become community lifelines as towns battle population decline
results.content: Declining birth rates and rapid rural depopulation across Korea have left hundreds of neighborhood schools standing empty, silent monuments to a shifting demographic landscape. But instead of leaving these idle facilities to decay into local eyesores, regional authorities are increasingly turning closed campuses into vital community lifelines. The Ministry of the Interior and Safety and the Ministry of Education on Monday jointly announced the winners of the government's inaugural contest recognizing outstanding repurposing of abandoned schools. Out of 62 submissions nationwide, seven projects were selected for financial grants and national recognition, highlighting how creative adaptive reuse can help rural communities combat population decline while offering urban centers new cultural infrastructure. results.title: Banks ramp up cybersecurity budgets for 2027 following hacking spree
results.content: Korea's major banks are sharply increasing their cybersecurity budgets for next year following a series of hacking incidents, with some lenders planning to spend more than 100 billion won ($74 million) on information security, data showed Monday. According to data submitted by the country's four major banks to Rep. Lee Yang-soo of the main opposition People Power Party, Shinhan Bank plans to allocate 115 billion won to information security in 2027, nearly 2.8 times its budget of 40.6 billion won this year. Hana Bank has set its budget at 100.1 billion won, while Woori Bank plans to spend 76.3 billion won. KB Kookmin Bank is also considering raising its allocation to more than 100 billion won, although the figure has yet to be finalized. results.title: 4 cheating cases using AI glasses caught at middle, high schools this year
results.content: Four cases of cheating using artificial intelligence (AI) glasses have been reported at middle and high schools this year, the education ministry said Monday. According to data collected from all 5,679 middle and high schools nationwide between Oct. 27 and last Tuesday, one middle school and three high school students were caught using AI glasses during their midterm or final exams. The middle school and one high school are in Seoul while the two other high schools are in North Jeolla Province and the southern island of Jeju. Three of the four were caught while constantly touching their glasses, while the other was caught switching to AI glasses after the exam got under way. In the latter case, the proctor had been keeping a close eye on the student following a tip-off from another student, officials said. results.title: Jensen Huang's Korean TV appearance with wife resurfaces amid affair scandal
results.content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's past comments about his wife are drawing renewed attention in Korea after he admitted to an extramarital affair amid allegations that he was targeted by Chinese intelligence. The controversy has cast a new light on Huang's appearance on tvN's popular talk show "You Quiz on the Block" in June, when he appeared alongside his wife, Lori, shared the story of how their relationship began. On Sunday (local time), Nvidia's board of directors announced an independent investigation following reports that Huang had allegedly been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The investigation will be overseen by a committee of independent directors with assistance from outside legal counsel. results.title: NK official's Beijing visit meant to share Chinese party meeting results, maintain high-level exchanges: Seoul
results.content: A senior North Korean ruling party official's recent visit to Beijing appeared to be intended to share the outcome of last month's key Chinese party meeting and maintain high-level exchanges between the two countries, Seoul's unification ministry said Monday. Yoon Min-ho, the ministry's spokesperson, made the assessment during a press briefing after Kim Song-nam, a member of the Political Bureau of the Workers' Party of Korea and a party secretary, visited China from Tuesday to Saturday, during which he met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and other senior officials. "(We) believe that the primary purpose of Kim Song-nam's trip to China this time is to share the results of the fifth plenary session of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and maintain high-level exchanges," Yoon said. results.title: More Korean Americans in Congress, fewer Republican allies: What it means for Seoul
results.content: The Democratic sweep in the U.S. midterm elections has added another Korean American to Congress, but the likely defeat of Republican Rep. Young Kim has raised concern among community leaders that Korea could lose a crucial bipartisan channel in Washington. Korean American members of Congress have long served as a bridge between Washington and Seoul, representing some 2 million Korean Americans, facilitating diplomatic networking and introducing legislation focused on Korea. Following the Nov. 3 elections, up to four or five congressional seats are expected to be held by Korean Americans. Democrat Dan Koh won a House seat in Massachusetts, becoming the seventh Korean American elected to Congress, while Democratic Reps. results.title: SK shieldus targets 100% renewable electricity this year
results.content: SK shieldus aims to source all of its electricity from renewable energy this year as the security company expands its emission-reduction efforts across its operations and supply chain. The plan follows the approval of its near-term emissions targets by the Science Based Targets initiative in 2025. SK shieldus said it was the first Korean security company to have its targets validated by the initiative, which assesses corporate emissions targets against climate science. Using 2023 as its base year, the company aims to cut its direct greenhouse gas emissions, known as Scope 1, by 99 percent by 2029. It also plans to maintain 100 percent renewable electricity use from 2026 through 2030 and reduce other indirect emissions across its value chain, or Scope 3, by 55 percent by 2033. results.title: Foreign tourist boom fails to lift Korea's tourism balance
results.content: Korea's tourism balance has remained in deficit for three consecutive months, even as the country prepares to welcome a record number of foreign visitors this year, with arrivals expected to surpass 20 million for the first time, government data showed Monday. Experts say Korea needs to move beyond one-off tourism packages centered on K-pop content and develop a wider range of attractions that encourage visitors to spend more. According to data from the Korea Tourism Organization (KTO), the country's tourism deficit — the gap between spending by foreign visitors in Korea and spending by Koreans abroad — widened to $498 million in September, from $399.4 million a month earlier. The country slipped back into deficit in July, ending a four-month run of surpluses. results.title: Germany's Henkel to open chip packaging materials R&D center in Seoul
results.content: German adhesives and materials maker Henkel will set up a research center in Seoul to develop packaging materials for artificial intelligence (AI) chips and high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday. The city signed a memorandum of understanding with the company at Seoul City Hall on Monday. Under the agreement, Henkel will make 12.1 billion won ($8.9 million) in foreign direct investment in Seoul by 2031 and hire 15 new researchers, including holders of master’s and doctoral degrees. The center, called Henkel Technology Center Korea, will be located in the Gasan Digital Complex, a tech business district in Seoul’s Geumcheon District. It will cover about 5,112 square meters, of which 1,205 square meters will be dedicated to chip packaging materials. results.title: Seoul subway stations turn into farmers markets selling regional produce
results.content: Five Seoul subway stations will host farmers markets through Nov. 28, where people can buy regional farm products at prices up to 30 percent below retail, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday. The pop-up market, named Seoro Itda Local Market, is run with five local governments: Ganghwa County in Incheon, Hongcheon County in Gangwon Province, the city of Gongju in South Chungcheong Province and Uiseong and Cheongsong counties in North Gyeongsang Province. In the name, “seoro” combines the first letters of Seoul and “local” and also means “each other” in Korean. “Itda” means “to connect” and plays on the English word “eat.” The market is linked to Seoul Pick, a program run by Seoul Metro, the city’s subway operator, that turns unused space in stations into pop-up shops for regional farmers. results.title: Questions arise over constitutionality, conflict of interest in special counsel probe design
results.content: A special counsel law passed by the National Assembly on Friday is drawing questions over conflicts of interest and whether its investigative powers are consistent with the government’s prosecution reforms. The legislation calls for an investigation into allegations that prosecutors and other state agencies fabricated evidence or brought politically motivated charges under former President Yoon Suk Yeol. Its 12 areas of investigation include cases involving President Lee Jae Myung, including alleged election law violations, involvement in development scandals and illicit money transfers to North Korea. results.title: Seoul district boosts crowd control at historic Namdaemun Market amid surge in shoppers
results.content: District authorities in central Seoul are stepping up crowd control and safety inspections across Namdaemun Market, where a social media phenomenon has driven an unprecedented influx of foreign tourists and young domestic shoppers into the historic commercial district. Jung District Office said Monday that it has intensified monitoring and field patrols across the expansive open-air market to manage heavy foot traffic, remove physical hazards blocking narrow corridors and position safety marshals during peak shopping hours. Long known as one of Korea's premier traditional markets, Namdaemun is seeing renewed popularity among younger shoppers and international visitors seeking bargains. The recent surge in congestion has centered largely around Hanyangsa, a small shop selling scarves whose proprietor gained widespread online fame for his witty sales pitch. results.title: Seoul adds downtown crosswalks to free pedestrians from underground tunnels
results.content: Navigating central Seoul on foot is getting easier as the city rolls out street-level crosswalks at major intersections, phasing out the labyrinth of underground passages and lengthy detours long forced upon pedestrians. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday that it has completed new crosswalk installations at Cheonggye 6-ga and Mugyo-dong intersection, while another is being built near Seoul Station, with opening targeted for the end of November. At Cheonggye 6-ga, the installation ends a nearly 20-year wait for a street-level crossing. Requests for the crosswalk date to 2006 but faced delays over concerns about the impact on underground shopping areas and nearby cultural heritage sites. results.title: Police chief nominee defends attendance at Cabinet meetings
results.content: Kim Jong-chul, nominee for commissioner general of the Korean National Police Agency (KNPA), said Monday that the police chief's attendance at Cabinet meetings is necessary and would not compromise the independence of police investigations and their political neutrality. The KNPA chief, who is not a member of the State Council, had not traditionally attended Cabinet meetings, but Kim has attended the meetings in his capacity as acting KNPA chief under President Lee Jae Myung's administration. Kim Ji-yong, the inaugural chief of the Serious Crime Investigation Agency, and acting Prosecutor General Lee Jeong-hyun have also attended Cabinet meetings, presided over by Lee, despite opposition criticism that their presence could undermine the political neutrality and independence of their respective agencies. results.title: Seoul Autumn Festa offers cultural escape to students finishing college entrance exams
results.content: Once college entrance exams are behind them, students in Seoul will have more than textbooks and university applications to think about, as Seoul’s autumn arts festival offers performances, discounts and cultural events to mark the end of the academic year. The Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture said Monday that its 2026 Seoul Autumn Festa is offering special ticket discounts and events linking performances with local businesses, particularly targeting students finishing the College Scholastic Ability Test on Nov. 19. Running through Nov. 29, the 73-day festival began Sept. 18 under the theme “Autumn in Seoul, City Becomes Art,” bringing performances and cultural events to venues across the capital.
